readingInstruction: Read Ephesians 1:1-23. The first fourteen verses are one long sentence in Greek, a single burst of praise. Read it aloud if you can, and notice how many times Paul says “in Christ” or “in him.” Then read the prayer in verses 15-23.
settingTheScene: Paul wrote Ephesians from prison in Rome, around AD 60 to 62, probably as a circular letter for the churches around Ephesus. Together with Philippians, Colossians, and Philemon, it is one of the Prison Epistles. Ephesians has no urgent problem to correct. It is a sustained celebration of what God has done in Christ and what the church is. The first three chapters tell what God has done; the last three tell how to live in light of it.
observation: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places” (1:3).
“Even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him” (1:4).
“He predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ” (1:5).
“In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace” (1:7).
“A plan for the fullness of time, to unite all things in him, things in heaven and things on earth” (1:10).
“In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit” (1:13).
“Having the eyes of your hearts enlightened, that you may know what is the hope to which he has called you” (1:18).
“He put all things under his feet and gave him as head over all things to the church, which is his body” (1:22-23).
interpretation:
The opening is a hymn of praise, not an argument. Paul blesses God because God has blessed us “with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.” Every blessing is “in Christ.” The rest of the sentence unfolds the blessings in Trinitarian order. The Father chose us “before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless,” and predestined us for adoption “to the praise of his glorious grace.” The Son redeemed us: “In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses.” The Spirit sealed us: when we believed, we “were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance until we acquire possession of it.” Three times the refrain returns: to the praise of his glory.

Notice the scope. God’s plan reaches back before creation and forward to “the fullness of time, to unite all things in him, things in heaven and things on earth.” The mystery of his will is that all of history is heading toward one goal: the summing up of everything under Christ. Believers are given an inheritance, obtained “in him,” having been predestined according to the purpose of the God who works all things according to the counsel of his will. We were not an afterthought. We are part of a plan.

Paul then prays for the readers. He gives thanks for their faith and love, and asks that God give them “the Spirit of wisdom and of revelation in the knowledge of him,” so that the eyes of their hearts may be enlightened. He prays for three things: that they know the hope of his calling, the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, and the immeasurable greatness of his power toward us who believe. The measure of that power is the resurrection and exaltation of Christ: God raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above all rule and authority and power and dominion, and above every name that is named. “And he put all things under his feet and gave him as head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.”

The church is not an afterthought either. Christ rules the universe for the sake of the church. The same power that raised Jesus is at work in believers. When we feel weak, we are to remember that this is the power on our side.
connection: Romans 8:28-39 and 2 Timothy 1:9 speak of God’s purpose before the ages. Colossians 1:15-20 and Philippians 2:9-11 speak of Christ’s supremacy. 1 Peter 1:3-5 praises God for a living hope and an inheritance. Psalm 110:1 and Psalm 8:6 stand behind 1:20-22. John 17:24 speaks of the Father’s love before the foundation of the world. 2 Corinthians 1:21-22 speaks of the seal and guarantee. Revelation 5:9-14 shows the Lamb worshiped. Romans 11:33-36 is a similar doxology.
application:
Read verses 3 to 14 aloud as a prayer, slowly. Underline each blessing.

Pray for yourself the prayer of verses 17 to 19: that the eyes of your heart would be enlightened.

When you feel weak, remember that the power that raised Christ is at work in you.
prayerPrompts: Bless God for blessing you in Christ with every spiritual blessing.
Thank him for choosing you, adopting you, and sealing you.
Ask him to open the eyes of your heart.
